historical_growth.eps_cagr_note: EPS CAGR not meaningful: FY2020 (COVID, -26.6c) and FY2023 (accounting scandal, -59.0c) are both negative, breaking the CAGR formula at every plausible start year. FY2026 underlying EPS (per management, not GAAP) was 42.9cps, a stated 3-year CAGR of 26% off the FY2023 trough -- not used as a forward driver because it is a recovery-off-a-scandal-trough artifact, not a repeatable rate.
historical_growth.fcf_3yr_cagr_note: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (FY2022 45.6 -> FY2025 271.4) is inflated by starting from a near-trough year and is NOT used as the growth driver -- shown for completeness only.
historical_growth.fcf_5yr_cagr_note: Owner FCF was negative in FY2020 (-331.3) and FY2023 (-121.1), breaking the standard CAGR formula over any 5yr window including those years. A cleaner 4yr span avoiding both negative years (FY2021 232.7 -> FY2025 271.4) gives +3.92%/yr.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (historical anchor only -- see growth_divergence_warning; the forward path is guidance-built, not CAGR-extrapolated)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue DECLINED historically (-1.5%/yr 3yr, -3.7%/yr 5yr) by explicit management design (portfolio simplification: divested Cleaning/Catering/Laundries and the Keolis Downer JV stake to shed low-margin, high-risk revenue -- the JV exit completed 1-Dec-2025). Equity CAGR is also negative (-7.3%/3yr, -3.1%/5yr), driven by the FY2020 COVID loss, the FY2023 accounting-scandal writedown (NPAT -385.7m), and ongoing capital returns (dividends + buyback) reducing retained equity. None of the standard historical CAGR anchors are usable forward growth proxies for a business that has just completed its portfolio reset -- for FY2026 (2026-09-26 update) management issued its FIRST post-reset medium-term targets (4-5% revenue CAGR FY26-FY30, EBITA margin approaching 6% by FY30), which is genuinely new, credible forward-looking evidence this build now uses directly for the early-to-mid projection years, decelerating to a conservative terminal growth beyond the guided FY30 endpoint.
historical_growth.notes: Do not use reported FCF CAGR either: reported FCF swung from -A$173.6m (FY2020) to +A$430.1m (FY2021) to +A$55.2m (FY2023) to +A$439.6m (FY2025) -- an 8-year EBITDA range of A$82.7m to A$829.2m (>10x peak-to-trough) confirms this is a genuinely high-cyclicality name. Cyclicality risk is now priced through the scenario driver paths and probability weights (bear weight held at 25%), not through a WACC premium stacked on top -- see inputs.wacc_rationale.

scenario_narratives.base: Portfolio-simplification reset complete; FY2026 proved the first margin milestone (5.1% underlying EBITA, ahead of target); guided near-term revenue dip (1H FY27) modelled explicitly before ramping into management's own FY26-FY30 targets (4-5% revenue CAGR, ~6% EBITA margin); legal overhangs assumed to resolve without material cash cost.
scenario_narratives.bull: Guided targets are beaten, not just met -- Defence PAS, energy-transition and Facilities wins push growth and margin durably above the FY30 targets; legal overhangs resolve cleanly; buyback continues.
scenario_narratives.bear: A material cash cost crystallizes from the class action or ACCC case; the FY30 targets prove aspirational and margin improvement stalls near FY26 levels, echoing the FY2023 mispriced-contract pattern in a still structurally thin-margin business.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Downer EDI is a structurally thin-margin (historically ~5-6% EBITDA margin), plant- and fleet-heavy government-services contractor that has just completed a multi-year portfolio-simplification reset (exiting Cleaning, Catering, Laundries and its Keolis Downer transit JV) and, for FY2026, delivered the first proof point of that reset: underlying EBITA margin of 5.1%, ahead of the prior >4.5% target, with leverage at a comfortable 0.8x net debt/EBITDA. Management has, for the first time since the FY2023 accounting-scandal reset, issued explicit medium-term targets (4-5% revenue CAGR and ~6% EBITA margin by FY30, 9% EPS CAGR to FY28) -- genuinely new evidence this valuation now builds into the base case directly, rather than extrapolating a declining historical CAGR forward as the prior (2026-08-10) version did. Because roughly A$140-150m/year of IFRS-16 lease principal is a genuine, recurring cash cost of running its plant and vehicle fleet -- not financing flexibility -- this model deducts it in full from reported free cash flow to arrive at 'owner FCF' (A$271.4m for FY2025, the latest full year, versus A$439.6m reported FCF), consistent with how other lease-heavy names in this research library (2CC.NZ, TAH.NZ) are treated. Two live, unresolved binary risks -- a shareholder class action in mediation and an ACCC price-fixing case against its Spotless subsidiary -- keep the bear-case weight elevated at 25% rather than the house default of 15%, and both risks are priced through the probability-weighted scenario construction and driver paths rather than through a discount-rate premium (this build also corrects the prior version's use of three DIFFERENT scenario WACCs, which double-charged the same risk in both the cash flows and the discount rate). A single 9.5% AUD WACC is used across all three scenarios. Readers who believe the FY2026 result and the FY30 targets mark a durable inflection -- not just a cyclical bounce off the FY2023 trough -- should weight the base and bull cases more heavily; readers who recall that the FY2023 scandal also began as 'a few mispriced contracts' in a similarly thin-margin business, and who note that both legal matters remain genuinely open, should weight the bear case more heavily. The entry price is the buy-discipline anchor (15% IRR hurdle including the full 10-year interim owner-FCF path and net debt) rather than the terminal-value-only shortcut.
key_risks_to_valuation: Shareholder class action (FY20-23 accounting irregularities): mediation occurred Dec-2025, no confirmed settlement outcome as of Sep-2026 -- an unquantified cash liability not yet in the bridge
ACCC price-fixing proceedings against Spotless/Ventia: still pre-trial as of Sep-2026, an unquantified cash and reputational risk

FY30 medium-term targets (4-5% revenue CAGR, ~6% EBITA margin) are only one year (FY2026) into a stated multi-year delivery track record -- a repeat of the FY2023 pattern (thin-margin base, contract mispricing) would unwind the recovery thesis
~90% government-revenue concentration exposes the business to AU state and NZ central-government budget cycles, which management has flagged as a near-term (1H FY27) headwind
EMOS-to-PAS Defence contract transition is an explicitly guided near-term margin drag before normalising

FY2026 annual report not yet extracted into this repo -- balance-sheet and FCF anchors are one half-year (H1-2026, 31-Dec-2025) and one full-year (FY2025) stale relative to the 30-Jun-2026 fiscal year end; should be refreshed once the FY2026 10-K-equivalent is ingested

bridge.item: Anchor refresh (price essentially flat vs prior_version.price_then -- see current_price; net debt/shares unchanged, still H1-2026 balance sheet, FY2026 annual not yet extracted)

Revenue growth and EBITDA margin paths re-judged for FY2026 actuals (pro forma revenue -4.6%) and managements first FY2030 medium-term targets (4-5% revenue CAGR, EBITA margin approaching 6% by FY30) issued 20-Aug-2026 -- prior path was a stale, pre-guidance declining trajectory built before these facts existed

WACC corrected from three scenario-varying rates (11.0/12.0/13.5%) to one uniform 9.5% rate -- the prior per-scenario spread double-charged cyclicality and legal risk already priced into the differentiated bear/base/bull driver paths and probability weights (owner-fcf-adaptations.md section 7f, charge risk once)

inputs.share_count_basis: H1-2026 (31-Dec-2025) WANOS 668.2m is the flat anchor; Year-1 drops to ~647m to reflect the remaining A$165.6m of the up-to-A$260m buyback executing (program was ~37% complete, A$96.5m of A$260m spent, as of Sep-2026 per FY2026 results commentary), then a modest -0.3%/yr ongoing net reduction consistent with management's stated capital-return posture and 0.8x net debt/EBITDA headroom. SBC is fully expensed in the flows (house basis), so this share reduction is funded reduction (buyback cash), not an SBC-double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement 'Share-based payments' add-back A$3.7m; immaterial (~0.035% of revenue) for this ASX/NZX industrial contractor -- SBC-zero-adjacent market, row kept explicit rather than deleted per house convention
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (H1-2026 half-year report; latest available -- FY2026 annual report not yet extracted into this repo)
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.5% AUD WACC (risk-free ~4.3% AUD 10yr + levered beta ~1.0-1.1 x ~5.5% ERP), applied UNIFORMLY across all three scenarios. The prior version (2026-08-10) used differing per-scenario WACCs (11.0% bull / 12.0% base / 13.5% bear) stacked on top of already-distinct bear/base/bull driver paths -- this double-charges Downer's cyclicality and legal/governance risk (once in the probability-weighted scenario construction, again in the discount rate spread) per owner-fcf-adaptations.md section 7(f) 'charge risk once'. This build corrects that: cyclicality, the two live legal overhangs (class-action mediation, ACCC proceedings) and margin-recovery durability are priced in the FLOWS (see scenario narratives) and in the probability weights, not in a scenario-varying discount rate. A single, moderately elevated WACC (9.5%, versus a plain industrial default of ~8-8.5%) is retained relative to a generic AUD industrial to reflect genuine capital-structure and covenant considerations (BBB issuer rating, AMTN refinancing) that are balance-sheet risk rather than cash-flow-scenario risk.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): IFRS-16 lease principal (A$147.6m FY2025) deducted in full from owner FCF as a recurring operating cost of running the plant/vehicle fleet; lease liabilities EXCLUDED from net_debt (net_debt = borrowings less cash only, per company convention). D&A used for the cash-tax EBIT bridge in the component build should exclude right-of-use depreciation to avoid double-charging the lease -- da_pct_path is set to the ex-ROU D&A share of revenue consistent with the FY2025 filing note breakdown.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is immaterial for Downer's current portfolio (NCI A$178.6m relates to a legacy Otraco/other JV structure disclosed at FY2025 year-end); no separate NCI deduction applied. Reported FY2025 net income of A$136.7m is post-NCI and consistent with the flows used.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF for an operating industrial-services contractor (routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' row). UPDATE of the 2026-08-10 valuation -- see reconciliation block. Two changes from the prior build: (1) revenue growth and EBITDA margin paths re-judged for FY2026 actuals (pro forma revenue -4.6%, underlying EBITA margin 5.1% vs prior >4.5% target) and management's first-ever FY2030 medium-term targets (4-5% revenue CAGR FY26-FY30, EBITA margin approaching 6% by FY30, 9% EPS CAGR FY25-FY28, cash conversion >90%), issued with the FY2026 results on 20-Aug-2026; (2) WACC methodology corrected from three scenario-varying rates to one uniform rate, per section 7(f) 'charge risk once' -- risk now lives only in the scenario drirver paths and probability weights. Net debt, shares and owner-FCF anchors are UNCHANGED (still H1-2026 balance sheet / FY2025 annual FCF -- the FY2026 annual report has not yet been downloaded/extracted into this repo, only the results announcement narrative in the Analysis JSON and the H1-2026 half-year filing). Two live legal overhangs (class-action mediation scheduled Dec-2025, outcome still unconfirmed as of Sep-2026; ACCC price-fixing case against Spotless/Ventia still pre-trial) remain unresolved and are carried in the bear-case narrative and probability weight, not as a separate liability in the bridge, because no cash settlement has been quantified or confirmed. band_position in the output JSON (728.6) is a numeric artifact, not a meaningful reading: house (6.20) and street (6.27) weighted IVs differ by only 7 cents because SBC is immaterial (0.035% of revenue) for this contractor -- the engines 1%-of-IV collapse threshold is not quite met (gap is 1.13% of IV) so it emitted a number instead of null. Treat house and street as having effectively coincided; do not read 728.6 as a percentile.

bear.narrative: Class-action mediation (unresolved since Dec-2025) and/or the ACCC price-fixing proceedings crystallize a material cash settlement/penalty; the FY30 medium-term targets prove aspirational -- the guided 1H FY27 dip extends further into FY27/28 as the EMOS-to-PAS Defence transition drags longer than guided and AU state Transport-agency budgets stay soft; margin improvement stalls near the FY26 5.1% underlying level rather than reaching the FY30 ~6% target, echoing the FY2023 pattern where a thin-margin base proved fragile to contract mispricing; revenue keeps declining through Y3 without margin offsetting it.

base.growth_rates_note: Y1 = FY2026 actual (pro forma revenue -4.6%, already reported). Y2 = FY2027, reflecting management's explicit guidance that 1H FY27 revenue/earnings are BELOW the prior year with 2H recovery -- modelled as a small full-year net decline before the ramp. Y3-Y5 (FY2028-FY2030) ramp into and hold management's guided 4-5% medium-term CAGR (using the midpoint band, tapering slightly into Y5 as the guided window closes). Y6-Y10 decelerate from the guided rate toward terminal growth (2.25%), since FY2030 is the end of management's disclosed guidance horizon and extrapolating 4-5% for a further 5 years would not be conservative for a ~90% government-revenue contractor.
base.ebitda_margin_note: FY2025 actual EBITDA margin (reported) was 5.97%. Management's own 'underlying EBITA margin' metric (a narrower, post-D&A measure) was 4.4% FY25 -> 5.1% FY26 actual -> guided 'approaching 6%' by FY30. This EBITDA-margin path (a broader pre-D&A measure, consistent with the component-build convention used throughout this model) is calibrated to move by a similar relative amount over the same guided FY26-FY30 window, landing at ~6.85% by Y5 (FY2030) versus 5.97% FY25 -- roughly matching the proportionate underlying-EBITA improvement management has guided (4.4%->~6%, +36% relative) applied to the EBITDA base. Beyond FY2030 the margin continues a slow, decelerating climb (7.2% by Y10) as portfolio-simplification and tendering-discipline benefits continue to season, but at a much slower pace since this is beyond management's own disclosed target horizon.
base.da_pct_note: Ex-right-of-use D&A share of revenue (FY2025 total D&A 3.27% of revenue includes ROU depreciation; trimmed slightly to avoid double-charging the lease already deducted via lease_cost_pct_path).
base.narrative: Portfolio-simplification reset (exit of Cleaning/Catering/Laundries and the Keolis Downer JV) is now complete, and FY2026 delivered the first proof point: underlying EBITA margin of 5.1%, already ahead of the prior >4.5% target, with net debt/EBITDA at a comfortable 0.8x. Management's first post-reset FY2030 targets (4-5% revenue CAGR, ~6% EBITA margin, 9% EPS CAGR to FY28) are treated as credible but not yet proven -- the guided near-term dip (1H FY27 below prior year) is modelled explicitly rather than assumed away, and the medium-term ramp is capped at the guided range rather than extrapolated beyond FY2030. The two live legal overhangs (shareholder class-action mediation, ACCC price-fixing case against Spotless/Ventia) remain unresolved in the base case -- assumed to resolve without a materially disruptive cash cost, consistent with no confirmed settlement figure existing as of Sep-2026, but this is a genuine base-case assumption, not a certainty.

bull.narrative: Defence PAS ramp (post-EMOS transition), energy-transition transmission/substation work, and Facilities growth (Stockland A$500m, new water-sector and NZTA wins) exceed the guided 4-5% CAGR; underlying EBITA margin durably exceeds the FY30 ~6% target as tendering discipline compounds and the margin-recovery story proves out beyond guidance (mature EBITDA margin 8.2%); the class-action and ACCC matters resolve without material cash cost; buyback continues into FY28, shares shrink further than the base case.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight held elevated at 25% (above the 15% house default) because two live, unresolved, binary-shaped risks remain genuinely open -- the shareholder class-action mediation (scheduled Dec-2025, no confirmed outcome as of Sep-2026) and the ACCC price-fixing case against Spotless/Ventia (still pre-trial) -- and because this is a structurally thin-margin (~5-6%) government-services contractor only 2-3 years removed from a major accounting-irregularities scandal that began, by its own account, as 'a few mispriced contracts.' Bull weight trimmed to 25% (below the house 35% default) because the FY30 targets, while now credible management commitments backed by one year of delivery (FY2026), still require several years of sustained execution to durably clear 6%+ EBITA margin in a business with this margin history -- the base case already gives meaningful credit to the guided targets being met, so the bull case is reserved for beating them.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
